name: Surface-state hypothesis
summary: Bardeen's idea that electrons trapped at a semiconductor's surface can block outside electric fields, explaining why early field-effect amplifier attempts failed.
description: Bardeen proposed that electronic states at a semiconductor surface could screen an applied field; his published contact model included surface charge and space charge.
tier_reason: A major reusable result, process or system within its field; broader multi-field or multi-generation dependence on this exact referent is not established.

impact.note: An explanation used by semiconductor physicists that redirected work toward surfaces, leading to the transistor and passivation; implies tier 2, below the reviewed tier 1.

why: Attempts at Bell Labs to build a field-effect amplifier gave far weaker effects than expected, demanding an explanation.

places.note: String names only New Jersey; Murray Hill assumed as Bell Labs' main site

market.note: Commercial availability is not a milestone of a scientific knowledge result.

date.basis: Museum dates the proposal one year after the April 1945 experiment; the contemporary paper appeared in May 1947.

links.statement: Nothing links 1895 to 1946 in electronics. Did radio detector work lead to the semiconductor surface problem?
links.caveats: Evidence needed: Bell Labs histories naming crystal detector and radar rectifier work. This probably needs new entries in between.
links.finding: The specified 1895 node is a coherer-based aerial/earth receiver; the retained 1947 point-contact history mentions wartime semiconductor technology but does not trace Bardeen’s surface problem to that exact Marconi coherer. A coherer should not be treated as the later crystal radar rectifier.
